# Results — Study 491 (McClellan Oscillator)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **the
McClellan oscillator forecasts the index: when EMA19(net-advances) − EMA39(net-advances)
crosses up through zero from negative, breadth momentum has turned and a rally follows** —
encoded as a mechanical rule. The oscillator is built causally on a daily **net-advances**
breadth proxy; a long fires on the first close where the oscillator crosses up from a
non-positive value, entered at the **next close** (one documented lag), and we measure the
forward 5/10/20/60-day return on SPY. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes; traded instrument **SPY** (public, no key) |
| Breadth proxy | daily **net advances** = (# basket members up) − (# down) across the basket `['SPY','QQQ','IWM','DIA','GLD']` — a **coarse proxy** for true NYSE exchange breadth (see caveat) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| net_adv range | integers in **[−5, +5]** over 5384 sessions (5-name basket) |
| Entries | **528** mechanical McClellan up-crosses (EMA spans 19 / 39; warm-up 3×39 dropped) |
| Timing / costs | oscillator read on close of *t*; enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per trade |

> **⚠️ Breadth-proxy caveat (this caps the test).** The genuine McClellan oscillator is
> built on *exchange* advance/decline data (thousands of NYSE issues). We have no offline
> exchange-breadth feed, so we approximate net advances with a tiny basket of liquid ETFs.
> A 5-name basket is a noisy estimate of true exchange breadth and could blur a real edge.
> This makes the test **conservative against a false positive**, not against a false
> negative — but the headline result (the trigger is *worse* than random at every horizon)
> is so one-sided that a richer basket is very unlikely to flip it. A future run with the
> sector basket `XLK XLF XLE XLV XLI XLY XLP XLU XLB` (cached on demand) would sharpen it.

## The signal — McClellan up-cross vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch trigger-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = trigger − random.

| horizon | n | trigger | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (trigger−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 527 | +11.3 bps | 59% | +0.97 | +26.3 bps | **−15.0 bps** | +9.3 bps | −1.04 | 0.300 |
| 10-day | 527 | +28.2 bps | 62% | +1.52 | +54.6 bps | **−26.4 bps** | +26.2 bps | −1.34 | 0.181 |
| 20-day | 525 | +51.6 bps | 64% | +1.51 | +123.4 bps | **−71.8 bps** | +49.6 bps | **−2.55** | 0.011 |
| 60-day | 523 | +209.2 bps | 71% | +3.01 | +309.8 bps | **−100.6 bps** | +207.2 bps | **−2.20** | 0.028 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks vaguely respectable at 60 days
(**+3.01**) — but that is **pure beta**: long-only entries on an upward-drifting index
inherit the drift. Against the **drift-matched random baseline**, the McClellan up-cross is
*worse* at **every** horizon (Δ = −15.0 / −26.4 / −71.8 / −100.6 bps), and the
trigger-minus-random difference is **significantly negative** at 20 and 60 days (Welch
*t* = −2.55 / −2.20). The breadth-cross does not forecast the index — it actively
*underperforms* throwing darts. There is no positive signal to debate.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — trade each index on the SAME breadth up-cross

| ticker | entries | trigger | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (trigger−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 528 | +51.6 bps | +1.51 | +123.4 bps | **−71.8 bps** |
| QQQ | 528 | +90.8 bps | +2.20 | +163.0 bps | **−72.3 bps** |
| IWM | 528 | +41.1 bps | +0.91 | +114.7 bps | **−73.6 bps** |
| DIA | 528 | +46.8 bps | +1.47 | +116.3 bps | **−69.5 bps** |
| GLD | 528 | +93.1 bps | +2.87 | +100.5 bps | **−7.4 bps** |

The trigger underperforms random in **all 5 of 5** names — including GLD, which has no
plausible link to US equity breadth at all (the −7.4 bps gap there is the giveaway: the
"signal" is just whatever drift the instrument carries). No coherent cross-sectional edge —
the hallmark of relabelled drift.

## Geometry placebo — shuffle the breadth in time, nothing changes

The decisive "does the breadth-momentum structure matter?" test: permute the net-advances
series **in time** (keeping its marginal distribution exactly), rebuild the oscillator, and
re-fire the up-cross rule. If the real cross genuinely carried breadth information, the
observed return would sit far in the right tail of the shuffled distribution.

| test | observed up-cross 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY shuffled-breadth oscillator | +51.6 bps | **0.988** | 500 |

**99% of time-shuffled-breadth oscillators match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.988). The
McClellan EMAs carry no information beyond their marginal — destroying the temporal
structure (the entire point of a breadth-*momentum* indicator) leaves the result untouched.
"Breadth momentum forecasts the index" is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real bounce

On a deterministic tape where a McClellan up-cross is *planted* to precede a real forward
bounce (knob `edge`), the same up-cross rule behaves exactly as it must — so the flat
real-tape result is a genuine "nothing there", not a dead detector.

| planted edge | n | trigger | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no link) | 91 | +37.8 bps | 59% | +1.04 |
| **0.30** (real planted bounce) | 91 | +738.5 bps | 98% | **+18.84** |

With no planted link the control sits below the *t* = 2 bar (no false positive — averaged
over 20 seeds the edge=0 *t* is +0.22 with only the expected 5% of |t| > 2); a real planted
post-cross bounce lights up at *t* = +18.84 with a 98% win-rate. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The McClellan up-cross does **not** beat a drift-matched random
  baseline — it is *worse* at every horizon (trigger − random = −15.0 / −26.4 / −71.8 /
  −100.6 bps at 5/10/20/60 days; the Welch difference is significantly **negative** at 20d
  (−2.55) and 60d (−2.20)). The only positive-looking number, the 60-day one-sample
  *t* = +3.01, is pure beta — the upward drift every long entry inherits.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no residual edge once the drift you were always
  getting is removed; in fact the rule gives *back* some of the drift by sitting out of the
  market and entering at worse-than-random times. Costs only deepen the hole. The same drift
  is captured more cheaply and more fully by holding the index.
- **"Does breadth momentum forecast the index"? — BUSTED.** The shuffled-breadth placebo
  leaves the result intact (*p* = 0.988): a breadth series with its temporal structure
  destroyed does just as well, so the specific EMA19−EMA39 breadth-momentum geometry carries
  no forecasting information. The McClellan oscillator is a descriptive breadth gauge, not a
  forecasting strategy.
